name: Chubby Chernobyl
imitates: A big, buoyant foam attractor that passes for a stonefly, hopper or cicada and carries a dropper nymph through summer pocket water.
recipe: Black over tan 3 mm foam, two layers
Gold/amber and black Fly Enhancer Legs
Polypropylene macrame yarn, blended grays, browns and golds

steps.text: Staple two foam sheets together and cut matched strips about as wide as the hook gap so the two layers line up.
Lay a thread base on the shank, glue it lightly, and dub a small nub over the bend up to the point. Leave the thread hanging there.
Set both foam strips on top of the dubbing, butts extending half a shank length past the bend, and bind them down with three firm wraps.
Halve four strands of leg material and tie two along each side of the foam, centered on the lower strip.
For the wing, brush out and blend several colors of polypropylene yarn into one mix.
Cut a clump about 3 inches long and lay its middle over the tie-down point. Bind it with three stacked wraps.
Dub a tight noodle and wrap it in front of the wing base to wedge it upright, holding the wing and legs back.
Keep dubbing to the eye and back, stopping just short of the eye with the thread hanging on top. Add a drop of glue.
Pull both foam strips down flat over the dubbing and secure them with three tight turns of thread.
Tie in the front set of legs the same way as the rear set.
Tie in a second wing clump, dub a collar in front of it to prop it up, work to the eye under the foam, and whip finish.
Smear a little glue between the foam layers at front and rear and squeeze them together, keeping the ends angled slightly up.
Fluff both wings upright and trim them to about a shank length.
Shag out the belly dubbing, trim the legs a bit shorter than the shank, and round off the foam corners front and back.
